transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Um… honestly, what pushed me to make the appointment is this thing that keeps happening at work. I’ll start follow-up items after audits or after mentoring events—like an email I need to send, or a review note, or some form that has to be finished—and I really do mean to complete it. I’ll have the best intentions.

And then a few days later I’ll realize the final email never went out, or the note is still sitting half-done somewhere. It’s embarrassing, especially because in accounting you’re supposed to be the organized one. I mean, I can make a beautiful checklist, color-coded and everything—my sister jokes I organize the organizing—but then somehow the last step just doesn’t happen. That’s what finally made me think, okay, I should talk to someone about this.
Did you have similar problems with finishing tasks or forgetting the last step when you were a child, such as in school or at home?

Yes, definitely. I mean, I didn’t think of it that way at the time, because when you’re a kid you just think you’re “messy” or whatever. But my report cards in elementary school were always like, “She’s bright, but…” and then some version of lost assignments, rushing through the little details, needing reminders to finish work.

My mom still brings it up—she’ll say I could ace the test but forget the project that was literally sitting in my backpack. Which is funny now, sort of, but also… yeah, that pattern was there pretty early. And I apparently talked out of turn a lot too, according to those comments, though I remember thinking I was just being enthusiastic.
Do you get unwanted thoughts that keep popping into your mind even when you try not to think about them?

Um… I’m not sure I’d describe it that way. Like, I definitely get things stuck in my head sometimes—usually something I forgot to do or a conversation from work—but I don’t know if that’s what you mean by unwanted thoughts.

It’s not like… scary thoughts popping in over and over, if that’s what you’re asking. Sorry, I’m probably over-explaining. I guess I haven’t really noticed that as a main thing.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things?

I don’t know… I mean, I worry, sure, but I’m not sure it’s “excessive” or about a lot of different things exactly. Sometimes if there’s something unfinished, I’ll think about it a bunch, and then I’ll make a list to calm myself down—which, honestly, I have probably bought more notebooks than any person needs. I had this one planner with little tabs for everything, and then I couldn’t find the tab stickers, so the whole system kind of fell apart.

But, sorry, that’s not really what you asked. I guess I don’t think of myself as constantly worrying about everything. It’s more like certain things get on my mind, but I’m not sure if that counts.
Have you been feeling down or depressed much of the time lately?

I’m not sure. I mean, I have days where I feel kind of low or frustrated, especially when I’ve been dropping the ball on things, but I don’t know if I’d call it depressed much of the time.

It’s hard because sometimes I think, “Am I sad, or am I just tired and annoyed with myself?” Like last week I was trying to sort through a stack of mail on the kitchen counter and found something I meant to deal with weeks ago, and then that sort of set the tone for the evening. But that’s probably not exactly what you’re asking.

So… no, I haven’t really noticed feeling down most of the time lately.
Do you often interrupt people or blurt things out before they’ve finished speaking?

Yeah… I do that. I catch myself jumping in before someone’s finished, especially at work with the junior auditors. Like they’ll be explaining something and I already think I know where they’re going, or the answer pops into my head and it feels weirdly urgent, so I just say it.

And then halfway through I realize, oh, I cut them off. I don’t mean to be rude. It’s just like if I don’t say it right then, I feel like I’ll lose it. Which sounds silly, but… yes, I do blurt things out sometimes before I stop myself.
